solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: More than one dictator hinders journalist making return

indicators.note: making return tells us to read the pieces backwards, turning them round

parts.note: to hinder is to stop, so hinders gives stops
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is obstructed while trying to get back home.
explanation.walkthrough: STOPS then ED gives STOPSED; reading that backwards produces the plural of a tyrannical ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Despots are absolute rulers, so the plural noun covers more than one tyrant.

clue.text: Fool in Belfast party taking recreational drug

parts.note: the DUP, the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, whose capital is Belfast
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish political party member is fooled into taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe someone is to trick or deceive them, i.e. make a fool of them.

clue.text: Study is set up — that is to finish some time or other

indicators.note: to finish places the next piece at the end
in a down clue, set up means written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study
taken as written
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A student's room is arranged, then someone says it will finish eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine die is Latin for without a fixed day, so adjourned until an unspecified time.

clue.text: Signs provided by females ousting head

indicators.note: ousting head means removing the first letter

parts.note: something provided by females is women's

explanation.surface: Women replace a leader and see portents in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens are signs or portents of events to come.

clue.text: Mark finished in a B&B maybe

parts.note: a stop, as in full stop, is a punctuation mark
over means finished

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark has finished his stay in a guest house.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a break in a journey, so a bed and breakfast is an example of where it happens.

clue.text: God to support the likes of you and me, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks a soundalike: the phrase spoken out loud gives the answer

parts.words: to support the likes of you and me
parts.note: to support is to back, and the likes of you and me are us: back us

explanation.surface: A plea for a deity to stand behind ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: BACK US spoken out loud matches the name of the Roman deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus is the Roman deity of wine, the counterpart of the Greek Dionysus.

clue.text: Sarcastic piece, no good, about India

indicators.note: about means going round, so the other letters surround the letter for India

parts.note: a bit is a piece
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sarcastic article about India is judged worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting remark is sharp and cutting, much like a sarcastic one.

clue.text: Another one who is in form given marks?

definitions.text: Another one who is in form given marks?

parts.words: Another one who is in form given marks?
parts.note: a form is a school class, and a fellow pupil in it is graded too

explanation.walkthrough: 'in form' seems to mean playing well, but a form is a British school class.
explanation.definitionFit: A classmate is a fellow pupil in the same school class.

clue.text: Something in the blood that gets moorhen moving

indicators.note: moving means the letters of the bird are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Some instinct in the blood sets a waterbird going.
explanation.definitionFit: Hormones are chemical messengers carried in the bloodstream.

clue.text: Fish on to the table: way to go!

indicators.note: in a down clue, on to means placed above, so the fish comes first

parts.note: the skate is a flat fish
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Someone serves fish to the table and is congratulated.
explanation.definitionFit: A skateboard is a wheeled board ridden as a means of getting about.

clue.text: Shut up Italian writer at street festival

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means confined or shut in
Umberto Eco, the Italian novelist

explanation.surface: An Italian author is confined at a street celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecost, or Whitsun, is the Christian feast seven weeks after Easter.

clue.text: A word of thanks, having got men aboard vessel

indicators.note: having got, with aboard, says the next letters are taken on inside
aboard means placed within, like passengers carried on a ship

parts.note: TA is British informal for thanks
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, i.e. men

explanation.surface: Someone says thanks once sailors have boarded a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat, but here it is a blood vessel; OR, other ranks, is a common way to clue men.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery leaving the heart, the body's largest blood vessel.

clue.text: What could provide reductions to shopper primarily?

definitions.text: What could provide reductions to shopper primarily?

indicators.note: could provide says the following letters may be worked into something new, rearranged
primarily picks the first letter of shopper

parts.note: first letter of shopper

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of shop gives a customer price cuts first and foremost.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of REDUCTIONS TO plus S, the first of 'shopper', are rearranged, and the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A discount store is a retail outlet whose business is selling goods below usual prices.

clue.text: Sort of speech perhaps too sloppy

indicators.note: sloppy means careless and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A remark that perhaps a talk was too careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of speech' suggests the punctuation mark, but here it is the rhetorical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe is a rhetorical address to an absent person or abstract idea in speech or writing.

clue.text: Sermonised Pastor originally has got to

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word Pastor

parts.note: first letter of Pastor
to have got to a place is to have reached it

explanation.surface: A minister has finally arrived and delivered a sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach is to deliver a sermon, so the past tense fits sermonised.

clue.text: About to have meat and veg in holiday location?

parts.note: CA, circa, means about
a rib is a cut of meat
a bean is a vegetable

explanation.surface: Someone is about to eat meat and vegetables while on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean islands are a popular sunny holiday destination.

clue.text: Arrived at firm — head of accounts encountered inside

indicators.note: inside says the following pieces sit within the word for firm

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of accounts

parts.note: first letter of accounts
to encounter someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: Someone reached a company and met its chief accountant there.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to a conclusion or figure is to arrive at or reach it.

clue.text: Worker in factory needing a cloak

indicators.note: in places the worker within the factory word

parts.note: a mill is a factory
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A factory worker needs a cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantilla is a lace scarf or short cape worn over the head and shoulders.

clue.text: Big shots — they may gather at Davos

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket a skier is a ball hit high into the air
second meaning: Davos is a Swiss ski resort full of people on skis

explanation.walkthrough: Davos also hosts the World Economic Forum, so 'Big shots' seems to mean the powerful; it actually means cricket hits that go up steeply.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier is a cricket stroke that goes very high, and also a person moving downhill on skis.

clue.text: Beset by loathing, son's hidden quickly

parts.note: to be beset by something is to be in it

indicators.note: hidden means placed out of sight inside the other letters

parts.note: loathing is hate
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son, with 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A son, surrounded by hatred, quickly goes into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: In haste means hurriedly or rapidly.

clue.text: "To some extent, inhumane" — a term for a dangerous woman?

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A quotation calling a cruel label for a predatory woman partly inhumane.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is informal for a woman who has many lovers and treats them ruthlessly.

clue.text: Couples imbibing rum — in these concoctions?

definitions.text: Couples imbibing rum — in these concoctions?

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, taking the next piece inside

parts.note: to couple is to tie, so couples gives ties
rum means odd or strange

explanation.surface: Pairs drinking rum, wondering which mixed drinks it comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' reads as the spirit, which fits these drinks, but in the wordplay it means odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Toddies are hot drinks of spirit such as rum mixed with water, sugar and spices.

clue.text: Qualification of the First Lady accepted by everyone

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, held within

parts.note: all means everyone
Eve, the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: The US President's wife is welcomed by all.
explanation.walkthrough: An A level is the British school-leaving exam taken around age 18.
explanation.definitionFit: An A level is an advanced exam pass, an academic qualification in British schools.

clue.text: Blairite hated being "out" — wanting to be this?

definitions.text: Blairite hated being "out" — wanting to be this?

indicators.note: out describes letters thrown out of order, set loose to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Labour supporter of Blair loathed being out of office and longed to return.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of BLAIRITE HATED give the answer, and the whole clue describes one out of favour who wants to be restored.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rehabilitated is to be restored to favour or good standing after a fall.

clue.text: Musical group turning up — one in the groove?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians

explanation.surface: A band showing up, one of them in the groove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the groove' suggests music, but it means fitted into a slot in woodwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is a projecting piece of wood that fits into a mortise or slot in a joint.

clue.text: Gathering given drink with five abstaining

indicators.note: abstaining means doing without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: bevvy is British slang for an alcoholic drink
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A get-together offered drinks, except five people who are teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group or company of people.

clue.text: Special force releasing half the characters from custody

indicators.note: releasing means letting go of part of the word, dropping it

parts.note: having something in custody is having possession of it
the second five of the ten letters of the word for custody

explanation.surface: A special unit lets prisoners partly go free.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a body of people summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law.

clue.text: Lover's farewell number — entertaining end to concert

definitions.note: Lover is, with 's standing for is

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest inside

parts.note: nine is a number

indicators.note: end to picks the last letter of concert

parts.note: last letter of concert

explanation.surface: A lover says goodbye with a song that includes a concert finale.
explanation.walkthrough: VALE comes first, then NINE takes in T to give NTINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is a sweetheart chosen or courted on St Valentine's Day.

clue.text: Bird plunging into each lake non-stop

indicators.note: plunging into says the bird dives down inside the next word

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A bird keeps diving into every lake without pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means everlasting, going on without end or interruption.

clue.text: "Little woman should be keeping home." Pardon?!

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so home goes inside

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Little Women
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: Someone insists a small woman ought to stay home, and the listener asks Pardon?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pardon?!' reads as a request to repeat, but it is the noun for an official forgiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to people guilty of offences.
